reply:
You left off by correctly explaining that a green square is allowed when every triangle must be green: the requirement applies to triangles.

Apply that same idea to the earlier sentence, “Every star-shaped piece in this tray is red.” It requires the stars to be red, but it says nothing about the colors of other shapes. A tray with red stars and a red circle still fits the description. So the earlier conclusion that a red piece must be star-shaped went beyond what the sentence tells us.

That is the distinction to carry forward: knowing a piece is star-shaped tells us its color; knowing only that it is red leaves its shape open.
